text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.92% today despite oil prices holding above $96 per barrel globally, suggesting the decline wasn't driven by crude weakness. The stock had rallied sharply on September 1st and 2nd (up $6.70 over two days) as Middle East tensions between Iran and U.S. allies pushed oil higher, and today's pullback appears to be profit-taking after that run rather than new negative news—the company still sits 5% higher than two weeks ago.

The underlying tailwind for oil producers remains intact: Brent crude stayed above $96 today after Iran's strikes on Kuwait this week, and oil has gained 7% for the week overall. However, markets may be pricing in some uncertainty about how long these hostilities will persist, as Trump indicated the conflict won't last long—that kind of statement can temper the "supply disruption premium" that initially drove prices and stocks higher.
